titulo: Gérondif and present participle: The gérondif

aula.objetivo: Use the gérondif («en parlant») for simultaneous actions, means and condition, and recognize the present participle («un homme parlant») and the infinitive after prepositions.

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: the gérondif is formed with «en» + present participle. The present participle: stem of «nous» in the present + «-ant»: «nous parlons → parlant», «nous finissons → finissant», «nous prenons → prenant». STEP 2: exceptions: «être → étant», «avoir → ayant», «savoir → sachant». STEP 3: the gérondif refers to the SUBJECT of the sentence: «Je marche en écoutant de la musique.» (I walk and I listen) STEP 4: uses: simultaneity («Je mange en lisant.»), means («On apprend en pratiquant.»), condition («En travaillant plus, tu réussiras.»), cause («En arrivant tard, il a raté le début.»). STEP 5: «tout en» reinforces simultaneity or contrast: «Il travaille tout en écoutant la radio.» STEP 6: the pronoun goes before the participle: «En le voyant, j'ai souri.» STEP 7: negation: «En ne parlant pas, il évite les problèmes.» STEP 8: difference from English: English uses the -ing form freely («walking»), but French only uses it with «en».
blocos.comparacao: in English the -ing form is free: «he arrived running», «she spoke smiling». French requires «en»: «il est arrivé en courant», «elle a parlé en souriant». Without «en», the present participle in French is almost only written.

tabela.example: En prenant le bus, tu arrives plus vite.
En étant malade, il reste chez lui.

erros.errado: Je marche écoutant de la musique.
erros.certo: Je marche en écoutant de la musique.

blocos.enunciado: Say out loud five things you do at the same time using «en» + gérondif.
Turn an active sentence into the passive and a passive one into the active, out loud.
